items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: [SPEAKER_03] Do you still play a 13 key, Albert, Mr. Warner?

ctx.x: can go forward with. You can play that tone that you have to cultivate until you get a reed that will just fit you to give that tone. Let's say we were an oboe. I have an oboe here, an old time oboe. I played a little bit of oboe. Not played out. In my head, a old time oboe, the keys were open on it. Right down there in the middle of it. Yeah, that's right. And I tried the flute, too. I played a little flute.
Do you still play a 13 key, Albert, Mr. Warner?
Well, if I was to play, I haven't checked a clarinet for years. But you have a 13 key. I have a 13 key clarinet.
